reproduce.selection: Of the 200 test films, remove previous experiment film IDs, require at least three distinct human descriptions for each track and combined view, duration 12-65 seconds, both streams starting within 0.15 s of zero and ending within 0.5 s of file duration. Among the 59 eligible sources form all pairs differing at most 0.75 s in file duration. In lexicographic filename order for each pair, rank the SHA-256 bytes of reel-track-recall-1/<first id>/<second id> and take the first six pairs without source reuse. No selection by described content. Present lossless FFV1 pictures and float PCM audio to the shared cutoff in 8 s turns.
reproduce.uncertainty: Use examples/check_first_impressions.py for natural picture and sound recall. For crossover gaps and changes use paired whole-source-pair resampling with 20,000 draws; all four assignments and both conditions travel together. One complete response per condition; the interval does not capture run-to-run model variance. Failed reader traces for one candidate case were discarded, and the complete original prompt was replayed after the log reader was repaired.

reader: Local authenticated Codex CLI gpt-6.1-terra. Each session views every turn in order on an anonymous MCP server with no shell, filenames, sound-source options or human captions. Science prompt and delayed recall use examples/watch_first_impression.py. No raw WAV supplied to GPT. Every condition includes AST, YAMNet, CoNeTTE and the local speech reader. The optional Qwen3-Omni helper is unavailable by design in both conditions.
design:
Pair six sets of two previously untested AVCaps films, selecting by SHA-256 of the names alone among pairs with original durations within 0.75s. For all four picture/sound assignments in a pair play to the common floor eighth-second cutoff. No time stretch. Confirm decoded PCM identity for each soundtrack and decoded picture/timing identity for each picture across its two assignments. No source names or human captions enter the reader. For each assignment get a first impression and separate open picture and sound recall through end_of_view in a fresh local gpt-6.1-terra session. Compare the same packets with the shipped first view and a candidate emphasizing the available acoustic readings in the first JSON fields; preserve their provenance, original image payloads, source descriptions and the presented words. Keep the optional large generative waveform reader unavailable in both arms as in the preceding recall benchmark. Do not treat an unavailable optional reader as absent sound. Primary: with the same picture fixed, does a change from recording A to B move GPT's sound description toward the independent human audio-only captions for B and away from A? Calculate the mean of 0.5 * (A-A - A-B + B-B - B-A) over pictures, equal pair weights. Also test picture identity under sound swap, open recall on the twelve natural films, and resample source pairs together. Label exploratory breakdowns separately. Test silence, absent speech and suffix changes using real stdio. Do not promote merely for improving boilerplate wording or scores on one example.
Before interpreting the crossover scores, inspection of delivered media showed that ordinary Reel additionally displays pictures near changes in the soundtrack. Keep that ordinary presentation as an end-to-end measurement. In a separate isolation run choose the first picture in each predetermined pair and present only its fixed-time overview and current frame, plus the actual recording's spectrum and readings. Verify identical picture pixels, frame times, and complete viewing time across the two recordings before each reader is called. Run this arm using the shipped unavailability behavior, independently of the proposed fallback.
endpoint: For a fixed picture, compare each heard sentence with the human audio-only captions of its actual recording and the other recording in its pair. Average actual-minus-other cosine over all four assignments, then over pairs equally. An answer that follows only the picture has zero expected discrimination when its text is held fixed. Repeat with the seen sentence while holding the recording fixed. Human baseline compares one held-out person to other people describing the same source and all people describing the other source. Source films were originally viewed at full length by annotators, up to 0.75 seconds longer than a pair, plus rounding down to an eighth-second. No human watched the exchanged tracks. No known perceptual ceiling on these remixes.

reader_conditions.current: Original unavailability and the recorded source estimates, including CoNeTTE, in audio.scene.
reader_conditions.candidate: If the primary reader is unavailable, also expose the available CoNeTTE windows contained within the presented interval as sound_descriptions, with model identity, basis, and other_reader status. No score filtering or change to reader instruction, sound, sources, or images.

quote_check: For perceived-sound recall only, scan paired curly or straight double quotation marks. Case-fold words and compare the quoted token sequence with contiguous published confirmed words on any one recorded channel. Exclude possible_words. Counts describe evidence in the speech reader, not human transcription accuracy. Paraphrases and unquoted claims are unscored.
scorer: sentence-transformers/all-MiniLM-L6-v2, pinned in examples/check_first_impressions.py. Paired uncertainty resamples complete two-film pairs together. The natural-film equal-weight total follows the previous sight/sound recall calculation. Scores compare short descriptions. Percentages do not measure agreement of every sight or sound.

upstream.method: On each natural source pool only the fully in-turn CoNeTTE captions used for the fallback. Weight window cosine by its duration and number of channels represented, then take the difference to the paired recording’s human audio-only captions. This diagnostic scores a stream of local estimates and a free one-sentence GPT recall under different tasks.
